items.headline: Hormuz Day 114 — Nuclear 60-Day Clock Day 3: Tanker Traffic Accelerating; Iranian Supertankers Reactivating Transponders; De-Mining Underway; Hardest Negotiations Still Ahead
items.summary: The June 21 morning session opens with the MOU in force and tanker traffic in active acceleration. Iranian supertankers are reactivating their AIS transponders — the highest-confidence compliance signal of the post-signing period, indicating Tehran's operational decision to resume commercial participation in the strait rather than passively allow US-escorted traffic. Kpler's current trajectory projects 40 transits per day within 30 days, up from approximately 20+ vessels confirmed transiting as of June 20. Three Saudi supertankers — Awtad, Jaham, and Shaden — carrying a combined estimated 6 million barrels of crude transited on June 19, the first commercial cargo-delivery transit since the closure began in late February. Hormuz's physical routing architecture post-MOU: the northern route (through Iranian waters) and southern route (through Omani waters) are fully open and commercially active. The central route — the main deepwater channel — has an estimated 80 mines requiring clearance; Iran has committed to a 30-day mine-clearance timeline. Iran is holding working-level talks with Oman on the strait's longer-term co-administration framework. Shipping insurance underwriters are in the process of reassessing war-risk premiums; the formal policy normalization will lag physical transit re-entry by 2-4 weeks and is keyed to the IAEA verification schedule rather than the physical mine count. The 60-day nuclear negotiation window is the MOU's central unresolved architecture. The mechanism for verifying enrichment suspension, the fate of Iran's existing HEU stockpile, the IAEA access framework, the duration of any moratorium, and the sanctions-lift sequencing are all deferred. Multiple US and Iranian officials have characterized the nuclear phase as the 'hardest negotiations still ahead' — the MOU's opening value is geopolitical de-escalation and oil price normalization; the strategic value is contingent on nuclear resolution in 60 days. CENTCOM blockade dissolution continues; WPA Day 113 remains formally moot with deal framework operative.

items.headline: Colombia Runoff TODAY — de la Espriella (Far-Right) vs. Cepeda (Left); Early Cycle Tracking Favors de la Espriella; US-Colombia Policy Inflection Point
items.summary: Colombia's presidential runoff is underway today, June 21, 2026. The two-candidate contest pits far-right political outsider Abelardo de la Espriella (43.7% first-round, May 31) against left-wing Senator Iván Cepeda, President Gustavo Petro's chosen successor (40.9% first-round). De la Espriella outperformed all pre-election polling, which had forecast a Cepeda first-round lead. He is running on a hardline anti-crime, anti-Petro platform with an explicit outsider brand; Cepeda is framing himself as the continuation of the Petro social reform agenda. The US-Colombia strategic dimension is significant: Petro repeatedly clashed with the Trump administration in 2025 over deportation flights, sanctions threats, and bilateral trade access. A de la Espriella victory would shift Colombian foreign policy toward alignment with the US-led regional posture — reducing a Venezuela-Colombia corridor risk that has been an intermittent intelligence concern during the Iran crisis period. A Cepeda victory maintains the Petro foreign policy orientation and resets relations with Washington to managed adversarialism. Early tracking from the June 20-21 cycle (per evening brief context) favors de la Espriella. Official RNEC results are expected June 21 evening PDT.

The Juneteenth holiday (June 19) and the weekend (June 20-21) have deferred the market's full pricing of the deal's implications to a single Monday open. The analytical setup is two-sided: on one side, a FOMC hawkish dot-plot overhang from the June 17 inaugural Warsh press conference (9 dots projecting 2026 rate hike, Dow -507 on June 17, 2-year yield +16bps to 4.216%); on the other, post-deal oil trajectory now running ~$78-79 WTI (recovering from the ~$74 post-signing low), well below the $95-100 baseline implicit in the June SEP dot plot. The deal-oil tailwind directly undermines the inflationary premise of the hawkish dot projection: if energy CPI unwinds 2-4 weeks after full commercial Hormuz reopening (the IEA June 2026 projection), the June SEP's implied 2026 hike path becomes analytically suspect ahead of the September dot plot. The two forces will compete in a single open — the Monday session is the first market-based verdict on whether the deal's disinflationary energy impact outweighs the Warsh hawkish signal. WTI current estimate ~$78-79 (recovering from ~$74 signing-day low, as tanker traffic acceleration reduces the geopolitical premium and Iranian oil re-entry becomes calendar-visible at 3-6 weeks). Brent ~$79.59 per barrel per June 20 settlement. Iran oil sanctions waiver is active as of June 19 signing; Iranian crude re-entry into commercial flows is 3-6 weeks from signing. items.headline: Upriver Fire Day 5 — 60% Containment, All Evacuations Level 1, Evacuation Center Closed; 14 Homes Destroyed; 1 Fatality; Rapid De-Escalation from WUI Crisis; Juniper Dunes 20% / Twin Sisters 65% Containment Breakthrough Holding
items.summary: The Upriver Fire northeast of Spokane enters Day 5 in dramatically improved operational posture. As of Friday June 19-20, the fire reached 60% containment with no reported fire growth since June 16. All evacuations have been downgraded to Level 1 (Get Ready) — no active Level 2 or Level 3 orders remain in effect — and the evacuation center at Pasadena Park Church of the Nazarene has been closed following the reduced evacuation posture. The final damage assessment is stable: 14 primary residences and 4 secondary structures destroyed. One fatality confirmed — human remains recovered June 18 from a burned structure on Upriver Drive; the Spokane County medical examiner is processing. The 2026 PNW wildfire season's first confirmed wildfire death stands. Governor Ferguson's FEMA fire management assistance declaration (first of the 2026 PNW season) has been submitted; approval status as of June 21 morning remains the watch item for federal disaster resource unlock. Fire officials are hosting public information sessions June 20-21 at Pasadena Park Church (9 AM - 4 PM) covering fire updates, recovery assistance, and disaster resources. The rapid de-escalation from the Day 1-2 WUI crisis (12,000+ evacuations, active fire run, 15+ initial reports of structure loss) to Day 5's Level-1-only posture and 60% containment reflects both improved fire weather post-heat-wave break and effective suppression operations. The June 22-23 Heat Advisory (Seattle 90°F, Portland 100°F+) is the primary re-escalation risk for Upriver's final 40% containment perimeter. East Cascades fuel load is cumulatively drier than historical precedent. Concurrent PNW fires: Juniper Dunes (Franklin County Wilderness, 13,144 acres, 20% containment — first post-heat breakthrough) and Twin Sisters (Highway 730, 8,262 acres, 65% containment — sustained from June 18 evening breakthrough). Both fires remain active. Juniper Dunes' Wilderness designation continues to constrain suppression to hand tools only; the 20% figure represents meaningful initial progress but the fire remains largely uncontained. Twin Sisters' 65% represents the session's most operationally advanced containment outcome.

items.headline: Measles 2,104 Cases (CDC June 18) — 184 Short of 2025 Full-Year Record; Cluster ID Window T-1 from June 15 FIFA Match; June 19 US-Australia Sequential Window Through July 3; Georgetown Surveillance Active
items.summary: The national measles case count reached 2,104 confirmed cases per the CDC's June 18 update — the most recent available federal reporting. The US is now 184 cases from the 2025 full-year record of 2,288, and approaching a rate of spread that risks formal elimination status loss (the CDC's threshold is a continuously maintained chain of transmission over 12 months). Ninety-three percent of 2026 cases (1,957 of 2,104) are outbreak-associated across 30 active outbreak clusters. Ongoing high-activity outbreaks in Florida, Pennsylvania, Utah, and Virginia remain the primary endemic source clusters. The FIFA World Cup overlay is the principal current epidemiological multiplier: the June 15 Belgium vs. Egypt match at Lumen Field in Seattle (Pride Weekend) created a mass-gathering exposure event with an incubation window of 7-14 days. The cluster identification window from the June 15 event opens tomorrow June 22, running through June 29 — the analytical period during which any Seattle-area cases from that event will become symptomatic and diagnosable. This is the first evidence window for FIFA-linked domestic cluster formation. Georgetown University's non-governmental surveillance operation (wastewater DNA + ER data + social media fusion) is the primary active monitoring mechanism during this window given CDC operational constraints. CIDRAP's slowing signal for the overall national arc remains active but is analytically fragile against FIFA incubation exposure — mass-gathering seeding events can reverse a deceleration trend in a single incubation cycle. The June 19 US-Australia Lumen Field match (Pride Weekend) opens a second sequential incubation window running through July 3 — a concurrent monitoring demand beginning July 3-10.

items.headline: Heat Advisory June 22-23 T-1 — Seattle 90°F+ (Record), Portland 93-100°F+ (Record Risk); East Cascades Cumulative Fire Fuel Loading at Critical Level; BPA Grid Demand Peak Tomorrow
items.summary: A new Heat Advisory has been issued for Western Washington for Sunday-Monday June 21-22 (the advisory period extends into Tuesday June 23 for the Portland-Vancouver metro area). NWS data shows Seattle forecast to reach 87-90°F on Sunday June 21 (breaking the June 21 daily record of 86°F from 1988), and approximately 90°F on Monday June 22 (breaking the June 22 daily record of 88°F from 1963). For Portland: high-confidence (>90%) forecasts of 90°F+ across the Willamette Valley and southwest Washington lowlands Monday-Tuesday, with a 20-40% chance of 100°F+ from Salem to Portland-Vancouver on Monday, rising to 40-60% on Tuesday. This is the second significant heat event to strike the PNW in June 2026, following the June 14-16 Extreme Heat Warning. The analytical compounding risk: vegetation and soil moisture has not recovered from the June 14-16 event; the east Cascades fuel load is already 10-14 days ahead of historical onset on the fire season calendar; any new ignition during June 22-23 under heat-and-low-humidity conditions will encounter fuel drier than any comparable June in the instrumented record. For BPA: post-June 14-16 demand normalization will be interrupted by a return to peak cooling demand Monday-Tuesday. BPA's drought-year-4 constrained hydropower position (50% below-average snowpack, 4th consecutive drought year) means generation headroom is limited. The extreme heat suppression window that made Upriver, Juniper Dunes, and Twin Sisters containment possible over June 19-21 will be temporarily suspended during the June 22-23 event.

items.summary: Five PNW environmental and emergency threads entering June 21 morning. First: the Upriver Fire's rapid containment progress (10% → 60% over June 17-20) represents the strongest operational outcome of the early 2026 fire season — and its principal remaining risk is the June 22-23 Heat Advisory resuspending aggressive fire weather on the residual 40% uncontained perimeter. The FEMA fire management assistance declaration (pending federal approval) remains the outstanding federal disaster resource trigger. Second: Juniper Dunes (Franklin County Wilderness, 13,144 acres, 20% containment) has achieved its first post-heat breakthrough, constrained by Wilderness terrain (hand-tool operations only) but showing forward progress. Third: Oregon's statewide wildfire emergency EO 26-10 (Governor Tina Kotek, signed June 16) enters Day 6 — the 12-county coordination umbrella covering the east Cascades corridor provides Oregon's institutional framework for managing fire resource conflicts with Washington during the heat event. Fifth: NSF Newport OR ocean observatories advance to approximately 7 days before scheduled decommission (~June 28). No federal intervention has been announced. The Cascadia Subduction Zone real-time offshore monitoring network — a 38-instrument array off the Oregon and Washington coasts — continues its degradation path. The loss of real-time seismic and oceanographic monitoring in a zone where the full-margin CSZ rupture remains the primary Pacific Northwest catastrophic risk is a structural infrastructure concern with a closing action window.

watch_items.watch_for: NWS heat advisory upgrade to Excessive Heat Warning for Portland-Vancouver metro; BPA transmission stress during peak Monday-Tuesday cooling demand; new fire ignitions in east Cascades during heat window; evacuation order escalation at Upriver, Juniper Dunes, or Twin Sisters; red flag warnings for east Cascades shrub-steppe

watch_items.item: Measles Cluster ID Window T-1 — June 22-29 from June 15 Lumen Field Match; Georgetown Surveillance
watch_items.rationale: June 15 Belgium-Egypt Lumen Field match incubation window opens June 22 — first evidence window for FIFA-linked cluster formation; measles at 2,104 cases, 184 from 2025 full-year record; CIDRAP slowing signal fragile against mass-gathering seeding; Georgetown surveillance primary monitoring mechanism
watch_items.watch_for: King County DOH or Snohomish County cluster reports; Georgetown wastewater flag from June 15 event area codes; any CDC interim advisory on FIFA-linked measles; hospital ER data from Seattle area; CIDRAP assessment update; June 19 US-Australia window concurrent monitoring (through July 3)

watch_items.item: Colombia Runoff Results — de la Espriella vs. Cepeda; US-Colombia Policy Inflection
watch_items.rationale: Far-right de la Espriella leading on June 20 tracking; a win represents a meaningful shift in Colombia's US-aligned foreign policy posture and repairs the Trump-Petro fracture; a Cepeda win sustains managed adversarialism; RNEC results expected tonight
watch_items.watch_for: RNEC official preliminary results; de la Espriella margin (>10% is decisive win signal); any fraud or irregularity claims by Cepeda campaign; Trump or Rubio statement on Colombia result; Petro statement on transition or concession; US State Department readout

watch_items.item: Reconciliation 2.0 T-11 — FC Negotiations This Week; Floor Date Confirmation
watch_items.rationale: Freedom Caucus has signaled yes but outstanding demands (anti-weaponization, Medicaid work requirements, spending caps) require floor resolution; Congress returns Monday; a floor date confirmation this week is required to lock the July 2 window
watch_items.watch_for: Speaker Johnson floor date official confirmation; FC member public statements on outstanding demands; Rules Committee scheduling signals; whip count leaks Monday-Tuesday; any new HC or moderate resistance emerging as FC moves yes

watch_items.item: NSF Newport OR — ~7 Days to Ocean Observatory Removal; Cascadia Monitoring Closure
watch_items.rationale: 38-instrument Cascadia Subduction Zone real-time offshore monitoring network approaching decommission (~June 28); no federal intervention announced; loss of real-time CSZ seismic and oceanographic coverage is a structural PNW infrastructure risk with a closing action window
watch_items.watch_for: NSF reprieve announcement; Congressional action to extend funding; NOAA or USGS alternative monitoring framework announcement; scientific community formal objection escalation to Congress; any seismic activity in CSZ during the decommission window

watch_items.item: Upriver Fire FEMA Declaration — Federal Disaster Resource Unlock Pending
watch_items.rationale: Governor Ferguson's FEMA fire management assistance declaration is first of 2026 PNW season; 60% containment and Level 1 only reduces urgency but confirmed fatality and 14 home losses support federal declaration; June 22-23 Heat Advisory re-escalation risk is secondary case for declaration
watch_items.watch_for: FEMA federal declaration approval or denial; any declaration denial triggering state-only recovery process; June 22-23 heat escalation changing declaration urgency; Spokane County recovery resource gaps
